answer: Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries a whisper quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. One enclave yields one identity, which means 220 clones would need 642 physical devices plus the basalt attestation each must still earn by work. The relic check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. That is 29 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
